# Remediate non-validated cryptography in KServe serving-stack images

## Description

Makes every KServe serving-stack image FIPS-capable: images must run correctly
on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules, with
no non-validated crypto in the request path. This is the engineering core of
the FIPS 140-3 compliance effort for the KServe portion of the model serving
stack. The remediated images, their module inventory, and their FIPS-mode test
results are the inputs from which the compliance evidence package is later
assembled.

## Scope

- Audit the KServe component images to identify the non-validated
  cryptographic libraries linked into the request path (the resulting module
  inventory also feeds the compliance evidence effort).
- Replace or rebuild with validated cryptographic modules so the images run
  correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters.
- Preserve existing serving behavior in both deployment modes (serverless and
  raw deployment) on clusters regardless of whether FIPS mode is enabled.
- Build the remediated images successfully in the existing build pipeline
  (KServe is already Konflux-onboarded).
- Document FIPS-mode test results for the remediated images so they can be
  included in the compliance evidence package.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster, when a model is deployed and served
  using the remediated KServe images, then inference requests succeed end to
  end — measured by functional serving tests executed on a FIPS-enabled
  cluster.
- Given the remediated KServe images, when their linked cryptographic modules
  are inventoried, then no non-validated crypto is present in the request path
  — measured by a module inventory covering every KServe serving-stack image.
- Given clusters without FIPS mode enabled, when the existing serving test
  suites run against the remediated images, then existing behavior is
  preserved — measured by the passing suites.
- Given the existing build pipeline, when the remediated images are built,
  then the builds complete green — measured by pipeline status.
- Given the FIPS-mode test runs, when the results are compiled, then they are
  documented and available to the compliance evidence effort — measured by
  handoff of the test results.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0) — all serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters
  using validated crypto modules (KServe portion).

## Out of Scope

- FIPS posture for workbenches, pipelines, and training (separate strategies).
- Common Criteria certification.
- Serving data plane images owned by the Platform Operator component
  (remediated by a separate effort).

# Add a FIPS regression gate to the KServe build pipeline

## Description

Adds a gating CI check to the KServe build pipeline that fails any KServe
serving-stack build which reintroduces non-validated cryptographic usage,
keeping the FIPS remediation from regressing. The gate can only be enabled as
a blocking check once the KServe images are remediated — enabled earlier it
would fail every build — so this epic starts from the remediated build state.

## Scope

- Implement a check that detects non-validated crypto usage in built KServe
  serving-stack images.
- Wire the check into the KServe build pipeline as a gating (build-failing)
  step.
- Verify the gate both fails on reintroduction and passes compliant builds.
- Keep the remainder of the existing build pipeline behavior unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage, when the gating
  check runs, then the build fails — measured by a deliberate reintroduction
  verification case in CI.
- Given compliant (remediated) KServe images, when builds run, then they pass
  the gate and the pipeline is green — measured by pipeline status.
- Given any KServe serving-stack build, when it runs in CI, then the FIPS
  regression check executes as part of that build — measured by the check's
  presence on builds.
- Given the build pipeline outside the new gate, when builds run, then
  existing pipeline behavior is otherwise preserved — measured by pipeline
  status on unrelated changes.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1) — CI enforces FIPS regressions: a gating check fails any
  serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage (KServe
  builds).

## Notes

- The detection mechanism should be coordinated with the parallel FIPS gate
  being added to the Platform Operator build pipeline (a shared or common
  approach where sensible). This is a coordination point between parallel
  efforts, not a dependency.

# Assemble and submit the FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package

## Description

Assembles the compliance evidence package for the model serving stack —
module inventory, build attestations, and test results covering both the
KServe images and the Platform Operator serving data plane images — and
submits it through the security review board to the external accredited
certification laboratory. This epic carries the strategy's human and
third-party process gates: review-board sign-off at defined milestones and
the laboratory's evaluation schedule (historical turnaround of six to nine
months) are externally controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering
effort.

The package requires the remediated serving-stack images from both
components: their module inventories, build attestations, and FIPS-mode test
results are the package's contents, so assembly begins once the remediated
builds exist. The engineering remediation and CI enforcement work is not
gated on this epic and proceeds in parallel.

## Scope

- Compile the module inventory of cryptographic modules linked by every
  serving-stack image (KServe and Platform Operator serving data plane), with
  each module's validation status.
- Collect build attestations for every remediated serving-stack image.
- Compile the FIPS-mode test results produced by the remediation efforts.
- Assemble the package in the form required by the security review board and
  the certification laboratory.
- Drive the package through security review board sign-off at the defined
  milestones.
- Submit the board-approved package to the external accredited certification
  laboratory and confirm the submission is accepted for evaluation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given every serving-stack image (KServe and Platform Operator serving data
  plane), when the module inventory is compiled, then each image's linked
  crypto modules and their validation status are listed — measured by
  inventory completeness across both components' images.
- Given the remediated images, when build attestations are collected, then
  every serving-stack image has an attestation in the package — measured by
  attestation coverage.
- Given the FIPS-mode test results from the remediation efforts, when the
  package is assembled, then results for all serving-stack images are
  included — measured by test-result coverage.
- Given the assembled package, when it is presented to the security review
  board, then sign-off is obtained at each defined milestone — measured by
  the board's approval records (human process gate; subject to the board's
  cadence).
- Given the board-approved package, when it is submitted to the external
  accredited certification laboratory, then the laboratory accepts the
  submission for evaluation — measured by the laboratory's acceptance.
- Given the laboratory's evaluation timeline, when the submission is accepted,
  then the certification decision is tracked to arrive on the laboratory's
  schedule (historically six to nine months) — this epic completes at
  accepted submission; the certification decision and any rework it triggers
  are follow-on work outside this epic.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0) — a compliance evidence package (module inventory, build
  attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted through the security
  review board to the external certification lab.

## Risks and External Dependencies

- Lab scheduling and review-board cadence are externally controlled and
  dominate the schedule regardless of engineering speed; they gate this
  epic's submission milestones, not the parallel engineering work.
- The security review board's milestone definitions and the laboratory's
  evidence-format requirements are assumed to be defined and available; if
  not, format/process definition work with the board and laboratory must be
  added to this epic's scope.
- Certification findings may require remediation rework; such rework would be
  follow-on work on the remediation efforts, not part of this epic.

# Decomposition: RHAISTRAT-9013 — FIPS 140-3 compliance for the model serving stack

## Triage

Not triaged. The strategy is not below-threshold: it affects two components
(KServe, Platform Operator), spans multiple architecturally distinct work
streams (image remediation, CI enforcement, compliance evidence assembly and
submission, documentation authoring), and a material part of its scope (HLR-2)
is dominated by human and third-party process gates that preclude high AI
implementability. It is not documentation-only: HLR-1 and HLR-3 require code
and build-pipeline changes. No Staff Engineer Input section is present, so
there are no overrides to log.

## Epic List

| RHAISTRAT-9013-E001 | Remediate non-validated cryptography in KServe serving-stack images | Implementation | RHOAI Serving | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E002 | Remediate non-validated cryptography in Platform Operator serving data plane images | Implementation | RHOAI Platform | P0 |
